reserves.name: AID reserve envelope (U.S. Treasuries and accepted stable assets)
reserves.issuerOrObligor: United States Treasury and GAIB-approved stablecoin issuers

reserveReview.rationale: Write-time re-open 2026-07-28: AID product docs still state AID is a synthetic dollar fully backed by U.S. Treasuries and stable assets and minted 1:1 by depositing USDC, USDT, and other accepted stablecoins. Transparency docs still point to aid.gaib.ai/transparency for real-time capital deployment and reserves status and describe quarterly third-party audits for portfolio disclosures. The public materials do not reproduce a current AID reserve component allocation among Treasuries and stable assets, so the complete envelope remains one unsplit basket with basket-needs-split. No inventing of category weights.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: GAIB AID product and transparency disclosures; constituent weights undisclosed
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The Treasury/stable-asset weights, stablecoin identities, custodians, and public assets-and-liabilities reconciliation are not reproduced in accessible source material.

nonLinkDispositions.reserveName: AID reserve envelope (U.S. Treasuries and accepted stable assets)
nonLinkDispositions.rationale: GAIB identifies the reserve categories but does not publish a reproducible current split among them.

Undisclosed off-chain reserve custodians (post-mint Treasury and stable-asset conversion)

custodyProfile.reviewer: Kimi P2 reserve cohort rc-2 (lead buidl-blackrock)
custodyProfile.uncertainty: GAIB documents the on-chain Minter and Redeemer contracts that accept USDC/USDT, but what happens to proceeds after minting — conversion into Treasuries, custodian identities, account segregation, insolvency protections, and reuse terms — is off-chain and undocumented. The June 2026 Spiceflow assurance report covers GPU-financing asset deployment, not AID reserve custody, and no AID reserve attestation is publicly retrievable.
